newsitem.title: ITALY: Glickman says EEP not ruled out, no decision made.
newsitem.headline: Glickman says EEP not ruled out, no decision made.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman reiterated on Wednesday that the United States had not ruled out restoring EEP export subsidies for wheat, but said no decision had been taken.
He added that Washington was monitoring market conditions and that while these had improved mainly for coarse grains, wheat still looked "a little tight".
"The best thing I can tell you is that we are watching it now," Glickman told Reuters on the margins of a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summmit.
"We have made no decision on EEP. We have got only limited monetary authority on EEP, $100 million," he said.
"Markets have actually in the past few weeks looked better. The crop report, especially on feed, looks better but wheat is still a little tight," he added.
"I have not ruled it (EEP) out," he said.
The U.S. Agriculture Department on Tuesday revised its 1996 corn crop estimate up by three percent from an earlier crop report to 9.27 billion bushels.

U.S. officials in Europe said Export Enhancement Programmme subsidies were not excluded, but played down the prospects of an immediate decision as long as the European Union stuck to a pledge not to undercut U.S. wheat with its own aid.
The EU recently resumed export subsidies for wheat but, in an apparent effort to a trade clash with Washington, pledged not to undercut export prices for U.S. soft red winter wheat.
